metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Windsor Heights, WV | Brooke County
metaDescription: Windsor Heights is a small Brooke County community with real mineral history. We trace the deed record and buy interests, including small fractions.
heroLead: Windsor Heights is small enough that a single old farm can account for a meaningful share of its mineral history, and that farm's original severance deed is usually still the document that matters most.
intro: A town this size in Brooke County doesn't come with a long list of separate mineral files — more often, a handful of original farm tracts were subdivided or sold over the decades, and the mineral rights under those tracts followed their own path, sometimes reserved by the original farming family, sometimes conveyed away entirely in an old deed.

We work Windsor Heights files the same way we work any Brooke County tract: pulling the deed record at the county seat in Wellsburg to confirm exactly what was severed, whether it's under lease, and who currently holds the interest.

sections.heading: A Small Brooke County Tract Base
paragraphs: Because Windsor Heights sits on a relatively small footprint, its mineral history is concentrated rather than sprawling. A small number of original farm severances account for most of the interests here, which actually makes tracing a specific chain of title somewhat more direct than in a larger, more developed town.
That doesn't mean the ownership is simple. Small tracts get inherited and subdivided just like large ones, and a farm that was one owner's land a century ago can now be a dozen fractional interests.

sections.heading: Windsor Heights on the Northern Panhandle Flank
paragraphs: This part of Brooke County sits closer to the legacy Gordon Sand and Big Injun shallow-gas history that defined the northern panhandle for most of the last century than to the dense modern Marcellus and Utica pad development further south. Some older wells in the area are still producing modestly, and some were plugged long ago without the paperwork being formally closed out.
We check current well status on any Windsor Heights tract before valuing an interest, since a producing legacy well and a long-dormant one aren't worth the same to a buyer.

sections.heading: What Changes When You Convert a Flat-Rate Lease
paragraphs: If your family's Windsor Heights interest is still under an old flat-rate lease and there's relevant production nearby, West Virginia's statutory 1/8 royalty floor may require that lease to convert to a royalty-paying structure. That conversion changes what the underlying interest is worth, which is why we check lease terms before making an offer rather than pricing off the old flat payment alone.
This applies whether the well in question is a decades-old shallow well or something more recent.

sections.heading: Tracing Heirs From a Windsor Heights Farm
paragraphs: It's common for a mineral interest under an old Windsor Heights farm tract to now be split among grandchildren or great-grandchildren of the original owner, several of whom may not even know the land was ever farmed by their family. We trace those fractional shares through the Brooke County deed and estate record.
You don't need to know your exact percentage before you contact us — that's part of what we confirm before making an offer.

faqs.question: Windsor Heights is a small town. Is my mineral interest even worth pursuing?
faqs.answer: Town size doesn't determine mineral value. What matters is the tract's production history and current status, which we check regardless of how small the community is.

faqs.question: I'm not sure my family's old gas lease is still active. How do I find out?
faqs.answer: We check the Brooke County record and current well status for your specific tract and tell you plainly whether a lease appears active, lapsed, or unclear.

faqs.question: Can you buy just my share if I have siblings who also inherited a piece?
faqs.answer: Yes, we buy individual fractional interests directly and don't require the rest of the family to sell at the same time.
